{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"defect","name":"ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): record_finding writes `fact_type: "finding"` and `basis: "measured"` into the merge on EVERY call that omits them, create or revise — so a revise silently demotes a defect to a finding AND turns a forecast into a measurement; the core merge is correct and is simply handed the default as if the caller said it","source":"art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL on the dev_storyflow field report (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27), triaged 2026-09-28.

① OBSERVED, verbatim (2026-09-25): "revising a TemporalFact with `record_finding` (same id, new `name` + `statement`, no `fact_type`) changed its stored `fact_type` from `defect` to `finding`. The tool's own contract is 'omitted fields keep their stored value'. Caught only because the reply echoed the node; a finding silently demoted from defect drops out of any defect-filtered reading." Expected: fact_type stays `defect`. NOT affected (per the hub's own observation): name, source, confidence, valid_from, statement all survive.

② PRECEDENT: fact:revising-a-finding-resets-its-fact-type-to-finding-2026-09-26 measured the same reset on 0.71.0 (status → finding) and said "Not root-caused: whether the default comes from the tool's parameter default or the store's merge was not read." No cause or fix recorded. Sibling observations of the class: fact:revising-an-epoch-without-its-description-clears-the-description-2026-09-27, fact:re-declaring-a-dependency-drops-the-resources-description-2026-09-23.

③ CANDIDATES. (a) The handler injects a default into the property bag when the field is omitted, so the merge sees it as supplied. (b) The core write replaces rather than merges (upsert_node not used). (c) A schema default for fact_type is re-materialised by the core on every write. (d) The observation is wrong: the reporter passed fact_type after all. (e) Not in record_finding at all: the reply is right and a later call changed it.

④ DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: create a fact with fact_type `defect` AND basis `forecast` (the second field is the refutation lever: (a) predicts BOTH reset, because both are written by the same `unwrap_or` shape; (c) predicts only fields with a schema default reset; (b) predicts every omitted field lost). Then revise with name + statement only, read the reply and get_node. Separately, write through a non-constructor path (replace_text) on a second defect/forecast fact. (c) predicts a reset there too, and (a) predicts none.

⑤ RESULT (reflow2-mcp 0.72.0, scratch store): create {fact_type defect, basis forecast, confidence 0.4, source, valid_from, value} → stored as given. Revise {id, subject_id, name, statement} → reply AND get_node: fact_type "finding", basis "measured"; confidence, source, valid_from, value kept. replace_text on the second fact → fact_type "defect", basis "forecast" kept. So (b) is refuted (other omitted fields survive), (c) is refuted (the core path keeps both), (d) is refuted (reproduced with the field absent), and (e) is refuted (the reply itself shows it). (a) holds. Source: crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/temporal_tools.rs, record_finding: `props = props.set("fact_type", req.fact_type.as_deref().unwrap_or("finding")); props = props.set("basis", req.basis.as_deref().unwrap_or("measured"));` then `upsert_node`, whose merge lets supplied keys overwrite. The defaults were written at birth (#447, aa799bd, 2026-09-07), two weeks after #302 made the tool revise-capable. Unchanged in current source (git diff v0.72.0 HEAD).

NEW BEYOND THE REPORT: `basis` resets too. A revise of a `forecast` fact makes it `measured`, turning a projection into a claim that something was observed. The 09-26 hub fact could not see this because its fact was already `measured`. Also: record_finding returns no `revision` block on a revise (the 0.72.0 sweep saw one from add_requirement, add_design_rule, add_capability, add_component, add_interface, add_constraint and add_decision), so nothing in the reply marks the two fields as moved. That is why the reporter caught it "only because the reply echoed the node".

⑥ CLASS: one of four ways a revise-capable handler bypasses the shared merge (fact:root-cause-the-revise-contract-is-implemented-per-handler-and-guarded-by-instances-2026-09-28). This one is a handler DEFAULT written into the merge bag. Fixing the two lines here would not have stopped the undated note or the add_verification refusal.

⑦ WHAT A PINNING TEST WOULD ASSERT (not written): create a fact with every optional field at a non-default value (fact_type defect, basis forecast, confidence, source, valid_from/to, value, steps), revise with id + subject_id + name, and assert every other property is byte-identical. A first create with the fields omitted still lands fact_type "finding" and basis "measured", as the counterweight.

PROPOSED FIX, the reporter's own "Opportunity" (09-25, first half: "keep omitted fields on record_finding revise"): apply the two defaults only when the node does not yet exist, the way plan_epoch already carries `status` forward. The reporter's idea is exactly this bug's fix, so it is recorded here and not as a separate Decision.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether record_finding has other revise side effects. From reading the code, HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT is drawn from whatever `subject_id` is passed, so a revise with a different subject may leave the fact hung on two subjects. This was read, not measured. `subject_id` is schema-required even on a revise, so "optional to revise" is not fully true for this tool (a minor instance, noted rather than measured further). Current source was read and diffed, not built.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: "changed its stored fact_type from defect to finding … the tool's own contract is 'omitted fields keep their stored value'" — CONFIRMED. Extended: basis is reset too.
